turns.prompt: does all tools have descriptions in spec?
turns.response:
Yes—based on the tool definitions inspected, every registered `ToolDefinition` has a tool-level `description` field. `ToolDefinition` itself requires `name`, `description`, and `parameters` (`services/agentd-py/agentd/tools/registry.py:16-19`). This holds across the built-ins, planning tools, session tools, web tools, sub-agent/team tools, memory/skills/todo tools, and MCP tools. MCP tools also receive a fallback description when the server provides none: `f"{name} (MCP server '{handle.cfg.name}')"` (`agentd/mcp/client.py:187-192`).

However, not every parameter/property has its own description. For example, `read_skill.name` and memory fields such as `content`/`query` are typed but lack property-level descriptions, while many built-in parameters do include them. So: **all tools have tool-level descriptions; parameter descriptions are not uniformly present.**
